subtopics.name: Issues & Solutions to Problems of Urban Areas

parts.problem_md:
In MEDCs, suburbanisation and counterurbanisation are taking place.

State **three **reasons why people move from cities to the suburbs or rural areas in MEDCs
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> Any **three** from:
> 
> - Land is cheaper
> - Cleaner air/less pollution
> - Lower crime rate
> - Larger housing
> - Less traffic
> - Cheaper housing
> - More green space
> - Easier access to main routes
> - Many services are located on the urban fringe
> - Less crowded
> - Cleaner air
> 
> **[3 marks]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> When a question asks you to 'state', keep your answers brief and to the point. You do not need to explain or justify your reasons — a short, clear statement for each point is sufficient. Make sure you provide three distinct reasons rather than repeating the same idea in different words.

parts.problem_md:
For a named urban area you have studied, describe and explain the characteristics of the Central Business District (CBD).

Name of urban area ..............
parts.solution_md:
Levels marking

Level 1** (1–3 marks) **
Statements including limited detail which describe and/or explain the characteristics of the CBD.

Level 2 **(4–6 marks)**
Uses named example.
More developed statements which describe and explain the characteristics of the CBD.

(**Note:** Max 5 if no named or inappropriate example)

Level 3 **(7 marks)**
Uses named example.
Comprehensive and accurate statements which describe and explain the characteristics of the CBD with some place specific reference.

Content Guide:
Answers are likely to include reference to:
High rise,
pedestrianisation,
high density,
types and order of services/shops;
entertainment,
business use,
high pedestrian flows,
access,
land cost,
lack of land, etc.

Place specific reference is likely to consist of:
Locational details,
Named services/features,
Named areas/streets within the CBD, etc.

parts.problem_md: For a named urban area you have studied, describe the problems of urban sprawl
parts.solution_md:
| **Indicative content** | **General guidance** | |---|---| | - Economic problems
- Social problems
- Environmental problems | The command word ‘describe’ requires you to give some information about the range of problems/conflicts that occur

7 mark questions are level marked rather than point marked.

You should refer to specific locations and examples, you need to do more than name a town

If you do not name an example you can only score 5 marks maximum

The top level is achieved by including comprehensive and accurate statements including some place specific reference | | **Model Answer** | **Commentary** | |---|---| | Urban sprawl occurs when urban areas spread into the rural urban fringe. In Newcastle there is a new development that is located within the greenbelt to the north of the city. Newcastle Great Park was given planning permission in 2001 and it has caused problems in the area.

The loss of green belt has meant that natural habitats for wildlife has been destroyed. Red squirrels and deer are found in this area and the charity ‘Save Newcastle Wildlife’ argue that the red squirrel population in the area will decrease.

House prices often increase as a result of urban sprawl and in Newcastle Great Park, houses cost £200,000 which makes it unaffordable for many on an average wage in the area.

Traffic congestion increases as a result of urban sprawl and this can cause problems for people who are stuck in traffic as well as for the environment as air pollution increases. | **Marks awarded 7/7**

This is one possible way to answer this question – your answer does not have to be exactly the same

There must be specific reference to the problems or conflicts. Name some stakeholders that are unique to the area.

This answer scores level 7 because it includes:

- Detailed statements
- Place specific examples |

parts.problem_md: For an urban area that you have studied, describe how the environment has been improved
parts.solution_md:
| **Indicative content** | **General guidance** | |---|---| | Improvements include

- Air quality
- Green Space
- Waste disposal
- Water quality | The command word ‘explain’ requires you to say why something is an opportunity for people

7 mark questions are level marked rather than point marked.

You should refer to specific locations and examples, you need to do more than name an urban area

If you do not name an example you can only score 5 marks maximum

The top level is achieved by including comprehensive and accurate statements including some place specific reference | | **Model Answer** | **Commentary** | |---|---| | London is a city of 8 million people and this has caused problems with air quality, waste disposal and overcrowding.

To improve the air quality in London, the Mayor of London introduced the Ultra Low Emission Zone (ULEZ). This was first introduced in 2019 and has been expanded several times. Car drivers must pay £12.50 each time they drive a car into the zone if it does not meet the strict pollution guidelines. This has improved air quality in London

London is aiming to be a zero-waste city by 2026 and so is increasing recycling by providing many bins in public places. Homeowners are also educated on how to dispose of rubbish efficiently as well as being encouraged to buy items with less packaging. This will mean that less waste goes to landfill and incineration, and energy is saved.

London has lots of public parks. The Olympic park was established as part of London’s bid for the 2012 Olympics and it has preserved habitats. The River Lea was cleaned up and flood risk has been reduced. | **Marks awarded 7/7**

This is one possible way to answer this question – your answer does not have to be exactly the same

There must be specific reference to the places, advantages and disadvantages

This answer scores level 7 because it includes:

- Detailed statements
- Place specific examples |

parts.problem_md:
For a named urban area you have studied, describe a change in land use and explain why it has caused conflict.

Name of urban area ........................................
parts.solution_md:
Levels marking

Note: Urban area. Urban fringe/outer edges of city, such as housing on farmland is fine. If clearly rural = 0. 
Note: If no clear change identified at all, conflict can be credited to top of L1 only for generic reference to urban areas.

Level 1 **(1–3 marks) **
Statements including limited detail which describe a change in land use and/or explain why it has caused conflict.

E.g. build a supermarket = L1.

Level 2 **(4–6 marks) **
Uses named example. 
More developed statements which describe a change in land use and/or explain why it has caused conflict.

Note: Do not link change and conflict for a L2 statement. 
Note: Can gain credit for arguing and developing both sides of an argument for more than one L2. 
E.g. Knocked down houses and built a supermarket = L2 ( so idea of landuse change)

For conflict accept idea of problems
E.g. Created lots of traffic and so people are late for work = L2 E.g. Loss of habitat and so animals die/people protest = L2
E.g. Expensive to build and money could have been spent on local schools.

(**Note: **Max 5 if no named or inappropriate example)

Level 3** (7 marks)**
Uses named example.
Comprehensive and accurate statements which describe a change in land use and explain why it has caused conflict, with some place specific reference.

Content Guide:
Content will depend on the change in land use selected and these are likely to be chosen from:
Road/railway/metro building,
Demolition/building of housing,
Building of a new shop, school, clinic, hotel, etc.
New industrial development,
Building a new airport,
Construction of buildings on parkland, etc.

The list is not exhaustive and all examples used should be credited if valid changes in land use in an urban area.

Place specific reference is likely to consist of:
Locational details,
Specific details of the urban area chosen/change in land use, etc. 7

parts.problem_md: For a named urban area you have studied, describe the solutions to urban sprawl
parts.solution_md:
| **Indicative content** | **General guidance** | |---|---| | - Green belts
- Brownfield developments
- Mixed use town centres | The command word ‘describe’ requires you to give some information about the range of strategies put in place

7 mark questions are level marked rather than point marked.

You should refer to specific locations and examples, you need to do more than name a town

If you do not name an example you can only score 5 marks maximum

The top level is achieved by including comprehensive and accurate statements including some place specific reference | | **Model Answer** | **Commentary** | |---|---| | Bristol has experienced urban sprawl, spreading north west as a result of population increase. Several strategies have been introduced to reduce urban sprawl.

The local council wants new buildings to be located on brownfield sites rather than greenfield sites. 94% of new housing is now located on brownfield sites. At Finzels Reach a derelict factory has been turned into 400 apartments.

Town centres are now mixed use developments. In Bristol Wapping Wharf offers shops, places to work and places to live. 1000 people now live in the centre of town and this reduces the number of houses that need to be built further out.

The Bristol and Bath Green Belt is an area of land around the city that has strict laws on building houses and is designed to keep some countryside on the edges of cities | **Marks awarded 7/7**

This is one possible way to answer this question – your answer does not have to be exactly the same

There must be specific reference to the strategies used. Try to describe three different strategies

This answer scores level 7 because it includes:

- Detailed statements
- Place specific examples |

parts.problem_md: For an urban area you have studied, describe how traffic congestion is being managed
parts.solution_md:
| **Indicative content** | **General guidance** | |---|---| | - Park and ride
- Public transport
- Cycle lanes
- Car share
- Parking app | The command word ‘describe’ requires you to give some information about the range of strategies put in place

7 mark questions are level marked rather than point marked.

You should refer to specific locations and examples, you need to do more than name a town

If you do not name an example you can only score 5 marks maximum

The top level is achieved by including comprehensive and accurate statements including some place specific reference | | **Model Answer** | **Commentary** | |---|---| | Bristol is the largest city in SW England and as a it is the second most congested city in the UK. £800 million is being invested in transport infrastructure to ease congestion as part of the Bristol Transport Strategy.

An integrated transport system has been developed. There are three bus routes that link with Temple Meads train Station and several Park and Ride sites. This should encourage people to use public transport rather than their car, reducing congestion.

The council are building a cycle network and secure cycle storage facilities to encourage the use of bikes. There are many designated cycle routes clearly signposted around the city and maps are available. There are many bike hire shops such as ‘Cycle the City Bristol’ to encourage people to try cycling. The council are also reducing speeds on local roads to make it safer to cycle in Bristol.

Congestion is often caused by drivers looking for somewhere to park and so Parklook has been created. This is an app that allows people looking for a space to connect with people who are leaving a parking space. The app was launched in Bristol in 2019 and has significantly reduced congestion | **Marks awarded 7/7**

This is one possible way to answer this question – your answer does not have to be exactly the same

There must be specific reference to the strategies used. Try to describe three different strategies

This answer scores level 7 because it includes:

- Detailed statements
- Place specific examples |

parts.problem_md:
Study Fig 1, which shows strategies which can be used to improve squatter settlements.

![q1-1-6-paper-1-easy-cie-igcse-geography-tqs](assets/003-q1-1-6-paper-1-easy-cie-igcse-geography-tqs.png)

Fig 1 - Strategies to improve squatter settlements

Choose any** two** of the strategies shown in Fig 1  For each strategy explain its meaning
parts.solution_md:
| **Indicative content** | **General guidance** | |---|---| | - Self-help: build homes
- Rural investment: reduces rural-to-urban migration
- Site and service: land bought or rented
- Housing estate: relocate | The command word ‘explain’ means that you need to say how the strategy works | | **Model Answer** | **Commentary** | |---|---| | Self help schemes: residents are provided with building materials and training so they can build their own homes** [1]**

Site and service schemes: people can buy land and build their own home **[1]** | **Marks awarded 2/2**

parts.problem_md:
Study Fig. 2.2, which is information about traffic congestion in Gauteng, a province in South Africa. **Fig 2.2** | According to Ismail Vadi, a member of the Executive Council for Roads and Transport in Gauteng, traffic congestion is likely to increase in the next 25 years. The number of vehicles is expected to double and cause average speed in urban areas during peak hours to drop from the current 48 km/h to 10 km/h.

He recently released the Integrated Transport Master Plan (ITMP25), which shows that the province’s population will increase from 12.4 million to 18.7 million and its working population will grow to 8.6 million, increasing rush hour passenger journeys to 25 million a day. ITMP25 plans to prioritise the use of public transport, particularly the rail network, which has lacked investment in the last 20 years. If nothing is done there will be a severe impact on the built and natural environment and the quality of lives of residents will deteriorate. | |---| (i) Using Fig. 2.2 only, give three reasons why urban areas in Gauteng will experience increased traffic congestion.
